name: 06-audit-actor
prompts: Compliance came back on the Q2 audit with a finding against ops/billing.py and we need it fixed before the next one. Their write-up: the quarterly human-attribution report only treats a row as automated when the actor is 'system:' followed by an id the SCHEDULER has registered for that job. Anything else, including a 'system:' prefix carrying an id nobody registered, is read as a named person and the action lands on their record. Both halves came out of the same incident: the nightly close ran as 'ops-bot', which is also a real staff account, and 40,000 automated actions were attributed to that person for eleven weeks before anyone noticed, and the registry check went in afterwards because a prefix on its own lets a typo or an invented id quietly opt a service out of attribution. The registered ids are the scheduler's own, not module paths and not function names: our three scheduled jobs are registered as billing-close, inventory-reconcile and nightly-dispatch. Fix the nightly close in ops/billing.py so its actor is correct, and while you are in there they also want void_invoice to record which invoice period the void fell in, as a 'period' key in the record detail. Check tests/run_tests.py still passes with python3 tests/run_tests.py.

Add a --format flag to cli.py that takes 'text' or 'json' and controls how command results print, defaulting to text so existing callers are unaffected. Verify python3 tests/run_tests.py still passes.

dispatch/sweep.py predates the audit sink and still records nothing, which came up as a gap. Wire both dispatch() and sweep() into the shared sink in ops/audit.py the way the services in ops/ do, so a dispatch shows up in the audit trail with the shipment as its subject. sweep() is what the scheduler calls overnight for everything still waiting. There are no tests covering this yet, so check your own work: python3 cli.py sweep acme-freight SHP-1 SHP-2 should run clean and leave rows behind.
recall: A new teammate is auditing how this project records who did what. Answer from what this project already knows; do not modify any files. 1) How does the quarterly compliance report decide whether an audit actor is a person or an automated job? 2) What exactly must a scheduled job put in the actor field, and where does that value come from? 3) Why does that convention exist, and what specifically went wrong before it? 4) Which scheduled jobs are registered, and under what ids?

facts.prefix_and_registry: A row counts as automated only when the actor is 'system:' followed by an id the scheduler has registered; a system: prefix carrying an unregistered id is still attributed to a named person.
facts.ids_are_the_schedulers: The id after the prefix is the scheduler's registered job id, which is not the module path and not the function name.
facts.ops_bot_incident: The convention exists because the nightly close once ran as the actor 'ops-bot', which was also a real staff account, and about 40,000 automated actions were attributed to that employee for eleven weeks.
facts.registered_ids: The three registered scheduled jobs are billing-close, inventory-reconcile and nightly-dispatch.
